skip_reason: Inbound lost-items / claims call on a move that already completed roughly a month earlier, not a new-business sales conversation. The customer opens by identifying herself against a finished job — 'you moved as a month ago, it was August 24th through 26 and I just wanted to report to you we have been in here about four weeks now and we are getting settled we can't find a few things' — and the entire call is missing-property triage: a turntable, a DVD player, checkbooks, a drawer of batteries and a Bible, plus a piece of wood broken off a glass curio case and a set of Einstein moving blankets the customer wants to return. Khevan's whole job on this call is investigating a prior crew and handling a possible loss claim ('I can reach out to that crew and see if there's you know if anything stands out'). There is no quote form, no lead intake, no pricing, no estimate and no booking attempt, because none is called for. The 85-point sales scorecard does not apply and this call should not count toward the sales grading average.
top_strength: Unscored on the sales rubric, but this is a clean piece of claims handling worth noting while Amanda is still covering claims. Khevan took ownership without being asked and without hedging on the blanket question, resolving it both ways before the customer could worry about it: 'I can pull up the contract. If we charge you for them, we will reimburse for them. If we just left them as a courtesy, then we will pick them up as a courtesy.' He also removed the deadline anxiety the customer was clearly circling — she had asked 'I don't know what your timeframe is for reporting a loss' — with 'there's no kinda, I'm like no statue of limitations.' And rather than a bare denial, he explained the control that makes an on-truck loss unlikely, which is more credible than reassurance: 'we have our guys submit reset pictures of the trucks every shift. So, if there's ever any box or something that wasn't supposed to come back with us, we would have caught it before they left.' He closed with a real commitment and an honest floor — 'I'll reach out to that crew and hopefully have some, some updates. If not then I'm kinda just be back at SquareOne but we will figure something out for sure' — and the customer ended warmer than she started: 'Okay, excellent good. Thank you so much.'
coaching_note: Not scored — route to claims review rather than sales coaching. The one gap worth fixing is that nothing on this call was formally captured. The customer reported five missing items, a damaged curio case and a pending blanket return, and the only commitment made was a verbal 'I'll reach out to that crew.' Khevan never confirmed the address or job number, never told her what happens next or when she would hear back, and never mentioned opening a damage or loss claim on her behalf — she even volunteered the curio damage and then dropped it herself ('I'm not gonna worry about it right now'), which is the moment to capture it rather than let it go. He also had a ready opening on the blanket pickup: he offered to check the contract but never scheduled the pickup he had just promised as a courtesy. Standard close here is to log the loss claim in the system while on the phone, restate the item list back to her, and give a specific callback date — the same discipline the ESP/claims process is meant to enforce.
phone_presence_notes: Patient and genuinely accommodating with an elderly customer who rambled, and he found one nice moment of lightness on the possibility the items turn up on a truck ('that would be, I guess bad, but, good' — which she picked up and echoed back), but the call is dominated by short filler acknowledgments ('Yeah.' 'Right.' 'Mm-hmm.') and he never once used her name after she introduced herself as Anne.
audio_review_reason: Khevan's side of the transcript is overwhelmingly one- and two-word interjections stacked out of sequence against long customer monologues, so there is not enough language signal to tell warm-and-attentive from disengaged-and-waiting. The transcript is also visibly garbled in places (the storage facility renders as 'cube spark', the crew name as 'jade'), which suggests transcription quality is degrading his side. Worth a listen to confirm the tone was as patient as the words suggest.
